definition.text: Input-derived terminal control describes settling and corrections after a static flick; it is not target-relative error without a reliable target track.

scope.text: Compare only the same metric version and matched static conditions, using the player's own distribution when no calibration exists.

mechanisms.text: Terminal adjustments can reflect task precision demands and movement control, but this observation does not identify a single cause.

forbidden_inferences: Do not label input-only corrections as visual overshoot.
Do not infer grip, muscle tension, or pain.
limitations: No absolute healthy threshold is available.
counterevidence: A matched run with equal outcome and lower correction burden weakens this candidate.

cue.text: Use one task-effect cue: arrive under control, then let the click follow the settled aim point.

dose_guardrail.text: Use a readable variant and change only one task variable; stop or reduce difficulty when discomfort or cue-unrelated quality collapse appears.

matched_retest.text: Retest later with the same static scenario, settings, metric version, and target condition.

near_transfer_retest.text: Retest later with only target size or distance changed.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Lower confidence or change the cue when matched evidence does not improve, near transfer regresses, or discomfort rises.

definition.text: Dynamic click error and acquisition-to-click duration describe target-relative click conditions only when visual tracking and outcome association pass their gates.

scope.text: Compare error and outcome within matched target size, speed, and change conditions; do not treat aggregate accuracy as target-state truth.

mechanisms.text: Moving-target control can combine acquisition, target-state reading, and terminal correction; the measured pattern alone does not select one mechanism.

forbidden_inferences: Do not call this reaction time.
Do not claim the player failed to see the target.
limitations: No visual gate means this entry must not support target-relative claims.
counterevidence: Stable error and outcome in the same condition weaken an acquisition candidate.

cue.text: Choose a readable moving target; identify its current motion, acquire it, then make one deliberate click instead of chasing a score.

dose_guardrail.text: Lower one motion variable first and preserve outcome quality; do not prescribe a universal duration or accuracy target.

matched_retest.text: Retest later with the same profile and motion-condition distribution.

near_transfer_retest.text: Retest later with one unseen target size, distance, or layout change.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Reduce the explanation to descriptive outcome when association or visual quality becomes unavailable.

definition.text: Speed matching is a teaching descriptor for persistent signed target-relative velocity mismatch; reading is a candidate training direction after validated target changes.

scope.text: Use relative motion only in aligned, target-identified windows. Predictive lead additionally requires segment-level predictability evidence.

mechanisms.text: Predictable and changing target motion can use different control strategies; a condition-dependent response is not a direct measurement of perception or intention.

forbidden_inferences: Do not equate reading with reaction time.
Do not infer visual attention or tension from mismatch.
limitations: Scenario predictability alone is insufficient evidence of predictive control.
counterevidence: The same mismatch without change-conditioned error weakens a reading candidate.

cue.text: On a long readable strafe, match direction and speed before committing the click; after a validated change, re-read the new motion first.

dose_guardrail.text: Vary one of speed, change density, or target size per block and keep hard variants as stress tests.

matched_retest.text: Retest later on the same motion script or matched change type.

near_transfer_retest.text: Retest later with one new speed, phase, or change sequence.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Do not use a prediction explanation when predictability evidence is missing; report a descriptive lead or lag instead.

definition.text: Predictable tracking compares error, coverage, and relative motion on sufficiently long near-steady segments.

scope.text: Phase and gain require an aligned steady segment; use descriptive error and coverage when this condition is absent.

mechanisms.text: Steady target-relative velocity mismatch can describe a control pattern, but it cannot identify sensory, muscular, or intent causes.

forbidden_inferences: Do not call phase lag reaction time.
Do not infer tension from speed mismatch.
limitations: Correction presence alone is not poor smoothness.
counterevidence: Matched coverage with stable error despite a different gain descriptor weakens a simple speed-matching explanation.

cue.text: Keep the relative speed stable through the readable segment and use small corrections rather than repeated large catches.

dose_guardrail.text: Use a readable script first and change only speed or phase when testing transfer.

matched_retest.text: Retest later with the same script, settings, visual profile, and metric version.

near_transfer_retest.text: Retest later with one phase or speed variation.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Fall back to descriptive error and coverage when steady-segment assumptions fail.

definition.text: Reactive tracking describes post-change error, loss, reacquisition, and return stability after validated target changes.

scope.text: Compare validated change types against matched player distributions and keep system alignment distinct from conditional response.

mechanisms.text: A higher post-change return cost is a candidate response-control pattern, not a direct measure of human reaction time or attention.

forbidden_inferences: Do not call this slow reflexes.
Do not claim the user did not see the change.
limitations: Detector loss must not be counted as player loss.
counterevidence: Stable return after the same validated change weakens the candidate.

cue.text: After the change, confirm the new direction, re-enter the target, and then restore stable tracking rather than forcing the old line.

dose_guardrail.text: Start with gradual or sparse changes and modify only change type or density per block.

matched_retest.text: Retest later with the same random condition and validated change distribution.

near_transfer_retest.text: Retest later with one unseen change sequence.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Remove response claims when change points, identity, or alignment are not accepted.

definition.text: Control tracking evaluates smoothness and correction burden jointly with error and coverage under a fixed metric, window, and filter contract.

scope.text: Do not optimize a smoothness score if accuracy or coverage worsens; intermittent correction can be task-appropriate.

mechanisms.text: Manual tracking can include intermittent corrections; smoothness metrics describe a trajectory property, not a universal quality score.

forbidden_inferences: Do not infer tremor, tension, or muscle activation.
Do not call every correction bad.
limitations: Short signals can make spectral measures unstable.
counterevidence: Lower correction burden with worse error or coverage is not improvement.

cue.text: Keep the aim path continuous while preserving contact; use only the smallest correction needed to stay with the target.

dose_guardrail.text: Use a smooth readable variant and retain error and coverage as guardrails; stop when discomfort or cue-unrelated deterioration appears.

matched_retest.text: Retest later with the same smooth condition and fixed processing version.

near_transfer_retest.text: Retest later with one target size or speed variation.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Stop treating smoothness as an improvement target when error or coverage regresses.

definition.text: A switching chain separates prior outcome, leave, transport, next acquisition, settle, and first-shot outcome when those events are observable.

scope.text: Use complete identity and outcome chains to separate transition cost from arrival control; otherwise report a partial discrete acquisition only.

mechanisms.text: Multi-target switching can combine movement transport and target selection demands; a chain does not reveal unobserved intended priority.

forbidden_inferences: Do not call consecutive flicks a complete switching diagnosis.
Do not infer a wrong target choice without observable rules.
limitations: Partial chains cannot support selection claims.
counterevidence: A matched layout with stable transport but poorer first-shot control narrows the issue to arrival rather than transition.

cue.text: Train transport and arrival separately: leave the confirmed prior target, move directly, then settle on the next target before the first shot.

dose_guardrail.text: Change only layout distance, direction, or target count per block and keep outcome quality visible.

matched_retest.text: Retest later with the same target layout and outcome rules.

near_transfer_retest.text: Retest later with one distance, direction, or target-count change.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Remove transition or confirmation claims when identity or outcome association is incomplete.

definition.text: Selection is analyzable only when the scenario exposes an expected-target rule; identity and proximity alone do not reveal intended or correct priority.

scope.text: When no rule is available, describe the chosen target and route without a selection-error or roadmapping claim.

mechanisms.text: Selection can be an independent sensorimotor dimension, but this product does not observe attention, intent, or game semantics by default.

forbidden_inferences: Do not label the nearest target as correct.
Do not infer planning quality from an unruled scenario.
limitations: Most workshop scenarios do not expose target-priority truth.
counterevidence: A declared rule and repeated violation are required before a selection candidate exists.

cue.text: When the scenario has an explicit rule, state it before the block and review only the observable route and outcome.

dose_guardrail.text: Do not add an unobservable planning objective; use the declared rule as the only selection variable.

matched_retest.text: Retest later under the same declared selection rule.

near_transfer_retest.text: Retest later with one layout or candidate-count variation while preserving the rule.

stop_adjust_rule.text: If the expected-target rule is absent, this entry must not produce issue, prescription, profile, or plan output.

definition.text: Tension management is a cue and candidate experiment, not a measurement of muscle activation, grip force, posture, or pain.

scope.text: Use only with a user report and one reversible cue change followed by a matched retest; retain competing explanations.

mechanisms.text: Kinematics alone cannot confirm a bodily cause; any benefit from a release cue remains a user- and condition-specific hypothesis.

forbidden_inferences: Do not say tension was detected.
Do not diagnose a muscle, joint, grip, or medical condition.
limitations: No EMG, force, posture, or pain sensor is available.
counterevidence: No matched improvement or increased discomfort rejects the experiment rather than confirming a cause.

cue.text: Try a low-risk release cue for one block, then compare the same condition without claiming a bodily diagnosis.

dose_guardrail.text: Change one cue only; stop immediately for pain, numbness, weakness, or persistent discomfort.

matched_retest.text: Retest later under the original matched condition and compare the outcome and kinematic pattern.

near_transfer_retest.text: Retest later with one task-condition variation; this is not a health assessment.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Stop the experiment for discomfort or when matched and near-transfer evidence do not support it.

definition.text: Without player movement, view, and target telemetry, movement aiming is limited to outcome totals and general input kinematics.

scope.text: This is an explicit unavailable boundary, not evidence for counter-strafe, movement sync, or movement reading.

mechanisms.text: No movement mechanism can be selected from the available sources.

forbidden_inferences: Do not diagnose counter-strafe.
Do not prescribe movement synchronization training.
limitations: The required joint telemetry is absent.
counterevidence: A future validated movement telemetry contract would replace this boundary.
